findings.summary: Map item 13 still promises 'listener auto-ref'; the contract makes it an explicit gap (message-port-ref-keepalive.md:92-96, Decisions :119) and defers the map re-cut to the land step. goal.md is unchanged and I4 does not state listener referencing (sweep reproduced: claimed path uses only manual ref/unref), so not a REV-10 axis-3 row; re-cut map item 13 at land so the map does not overstate delivery.

Fault row 2 enumerates the four native transfer entry points only. rifty's own worker_threads.Worker#postMessage(msg) drops Node's transferList and routes through workerHandle.send / a same-realm by-reference fallback. Final+GREEN sibling sweep should show no rifty-owned path (worker_threads Worker/parentPort, kernel send) can move a recorded port past the wrapped entry points and hide its release.

The planned MessageChannel Proxy and the postMessage/structuredClone/global-postMessage wrappers are realm-wide, and rifty-internal channels created after install are recorded too. Case 7 guards guest native transfer only. #351 broke BroadcastChannel this way, and @emnapi/core napi_detach_arraybuffer uses port1.postMessage(buf,[buf]). Final+GREEN should run the lanes that exercise rifty-internal port traffic, not only the new specs.

The newly added hasRef() will return false where Node returns true: on listener-referenced ports, and between close() and the close-callback phase. These are documented gaps (ADR-0447 §Explicit gaps, compat ❌/⚠️ via Acceptance 3), not loud throws. That is acceptable only while the compat rows land verbatim, so Final+GREEN should confirm the rows name the hasRef divergence explicitly.
